transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Um… well, I’m probably making it sound bigger than it is, but work has been really stressful. I drive for transportation, and I’ve noticed dispatch and compliance kind of… following my route changes in the computer system. And there are little comments on the radio that seem like they’re about me.

People keep saying it’s just normal oversight, and maybe that’s what you’ll think too, but I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. I just thought maybe I should talk to someone before it gets worse or I handle it the wrong way.
Do you believe for certain that your coworkers are intentionally monitoring or reporting on you?

I mean… “for certain” sounds kind of strong, and I don’t want to come across like I’m accusing everybody. But yes, I do feel like dispatch and compliance are tracking my route changes in the system, and some of the radio comments seem too specific to be random.

Even when people tell me it’s just normal oversight, I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. I know that probably sounds bad, but that’s honestly how it feels.
Have you heard voices when no one was actually there?

Um… no, I don’t think so. Not like a voice in the room when nobody’s there. Sometimes I replay what people said or wonder if comments were meant for me, but I wouldn’t say I’m hearing voices. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you used methamphetamine, cannabis, or any other drugs around the time these concerns started?

Um… no, I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not really into drugs like that. I know people ask because it can affect how someone’s thinking, and that makes sense.

I haven’t noticed any connection like that around when this started. I don’t want to give the wrong impression.
Before these concerns started, had you had a head injury, seizure, or other neurological illness?

Not that I know of, no. I mean, I’ve never had anything like a seizure or some diagnosed brain thing, and I don’t remember a head injury before all this started. If there’s a specific kind of injury you mean, I can think about it, but nothing stands out to me.
Is it possible that you might be mistaken about your coworkers monitoring or reporting on you?

I mean… I know it’s possible I could be misreading some things. I don’t want to sound like I’m accusing everyone or being difficult.

But it doesn’t really feel like I’m mistaken. The route changes show up in the computer system, and then there are little comments on the radio that seem connected to what I’ve been doing. And certain drivers… it just feels like they’re reporting on me, even if people tell me it’s normal oversight. I’m trying to be fair about it, but I can tell there’s something there.
About how long have you been feeling that your coworkers are monitoring or reporting on you?

Um… I’d say it’s been about two months that it’s felt pretty clear to me. Like the computer route changes and the radio comments seeming connected.

Maybe it was a little vague before that, but around the last couple months is when I really started feeling like, okay, this is happening. Does that answer what you mean?
Because of this, has your work performance gotten noticeably worse?

A little, yeah… I mean, I’m still trying to do my job, but I guess it has gotten harder.

I’ve fallen behind on some of the route reports, and sometimes the instructions I give aren’t as clear as they should be, so drivers have complained. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m not trying, because I am. It’s just been harder to keep everything straight.

And at home too, honestly… my husband has had to take over more things, like meals, phone calls, basic planning. I feel bad saying that, but I haven’t been keeping up like I normally would.
From when these concerns first began, has there been any stretch where they completely went away?

No… I don’t think it’s completely gone away. Maybe some days I try not to focus on it as much, or it feels a little less intense, but the tracking through the computer system and the radio comments have felt pretty clear to me for about the past two months.

I mean, I hope that’s the kind of answer you’re asking for.
Since this started, have you felt emotionally flat or lost interest in things you usually care about?

Maybe a little… I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But I haven’t really felt like singing with the choir lately, or having the softball team over like we used to.

Most days after my shift, I’ll sit at the kitchen table with my planner open, like I’m going to start dinner or make calls or get things organized, and then I just… don’t. I kind of sit there and can’t get myself going. Is that what you mean by lost interest?
Have these concerns about your coworkers been present for more than one month?

Yes… I think so. I mean, it’s not like I was marking it on a calendar at first, but the computer tracking and the comments over the radio have felt pretty clear to me for about two months now.

I know that probably sounds like a long time. I’m just trying to answer it the right way.
Have other people told you that your speech has been hard to follow or that your thoughts seem jumbled?

Um… not really, I don’t think so. Nobody’s said it that way to me.

Sometimes I feel like I’m trying to explain things and I can tell people aren’t quite getting what I mean, but I don’t know if that’s my speech being jumbled or just… it being hard to explain. Does that answer what you’re asking?
From when you first noticed any of this starting, has it been going on for six months or longer?

I guess… yes, if I’m counting from when it first started to feel off. It’s been about eight months, since I was put in that temporary dispatch lead role.

I didn’t think of it as a “problem” right away, so I’m not sure if that’s the right starting point, but that’s when things started building.
Have other people told you that your behavior has seemed strange or disorganized?

A couple people at work have kind of hinted that, yeah. Not like… “you’re disorganized,” exactly, but they’ll look at me funny.

Sometimes I get stuck rearranging the magnets and route slips on the board into a certain pattern, because it feels like if it’s not right then the whole board is going to go wrong. Or I’ll repeat the last few words a driver says before I answer them, just to make sure I’ve got it straight. People act like I’m being difficult, but I’m not trying to be. I’m really trying to keep things from getting messed up.

I know that probably sounds strange. I’m not trying to make excuses. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have there been times when your behavior felt so disorganized that you had trouble carrying out basic tasks at work or at home?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but there have been times.

At work I’ve fallen behind on the route reports, and sometimes when I’m giving instructions to the drivers, they tell me it doesn’t make sense or they complain that I’m confusing them. I try to fix it, but it’s like I can’t get it organized fast enough.

And at home… my husband has been picking up more. Meals, phone calls, just basic planning stuff. I feel bad saying that, because I don’t want it to sound like I’m not trying. I am trying. I’m just not keeping up the way I used to. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
